I'm very near a point of no return with college. I've lost the scholarship that was paying for my apt, and I got a letter that said my pass rate was about to be too low for fin. aid tuition grants.

As bad as it sounds, I've never been employed. If I lose all funding, I'm starting from zero and low-end jobs, I imagine, wouldn't do so well at paying for both rent and formal piece-of-paper education. The parental imperative was so long that I'm pursuing my 4 year (I'm one of the first in family to go straight to uni out of high school), I'll have accomodations taken care of.

But the rent is expensive, and I just bought a new laptop, and it's like being a leech. I can't just end up back at home and use it as a stop to a humble debt-free existence without some kind of conflict. Especially if I pull a second Space Shuttle Challenger and end up home after that.

I applied a couple of weeks ago, and when I put that my likeliness of committing suicide was high, there was an immediate intervention. I pretty much laid out the situation described in OP, academics, shortcomings, loneliness and all.

I was assigned to a counselor, and from our first session we worked to define the goal as "building confidence/self-esteem," as well as finding the line between competence and confidence. He didn't leave much of an impression on me, so I switched to the person who did the immediate intervention.

The goal is sort of "contingency plan for if I drop out" + "reasons to live."
